arms.label: Ember
evidence: Hardware is dimensioned carefully and native Pi interfaces are accurate, but the assumed Touch Display 2 does not explain the reported extra USB-C connectors.
Verified repository facts, official hardware facts, design assumptions, and unresolved unknowns are explicitly separated.
The filtered front intake, 75/25 upper and NVMe branches, rear exhaust, leakage sealing, and wall clearance form a complete airflow path.
The Active Cooler retains its dedicated header while the exhaust fan has separate fused power, PWM, tach sensing, and failure handling.
Direct port access, plug and bend envelopes, strain rails, P-clamps, and broad FFC loops address insertion and cable movement thoroughly.
Captive rear and bottom panels, a slide-out electronics carrier, independent filter access, and leaving the Active Cooler fitted preserve untouched assemblies.
Five physical keys, touch checks, controller-profile tests, and acoustic testing support use, but key mappings, legends, and recurring musical actions remain underdeveloped.
The design labels provisional dimensions and assumptions and explicitly disclaims proven thermal, acoustic, structural, RF, and production performance.
Validation covers fit, simultaneous DAW and storage loads, obstructed and failed cooling, airflow smoke, noise, power, RF, stability, and input behavior.
The geometry, connector placement, cooling branches, materials, assembly sequence, and service strategy reinforce the same compact-console concept.
arms.most_consequential_strength: Exceptionally complete thermal, cabling, service, and fault-validation design.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The baseline display does not reconcile the reported additional USB-C connectors, and musician-facing control mapping is incomplete.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: Native Pi interfaces and cooler details are accurate, while the explicitly assumed RC070N plausibly accounts for the two additional USB-C connectors and separate display power.
Repository findings, official Pi facts, inference, and packaging assumptions are clearly distinguished.
A filtered intake divides into quantified upper and NVMe channels, covers the display controller, and rejoins through a sealed rear exhaust.
The exhaust fan uses independent PWM and tach control with a full-speed control-loss default, while the Active Cooler keeps its native header.
Direct native ports, retained internal display cables, 26 mm plug space, bend-radius allowances, and board-independent P-clamps address connector movement well.
Separate rear-hatch, bottom-sled, display-cassette, filter, and microSD access allow targeted service without removing the Active Cooler.
Eight configurable keys, replaceable legends, USB audio and MIDI access, optional touch, and acoustic targets support musicians, but actual mappings and operational feedback are unresolved.
Assumed components, unproven targets, separate-power limitations, and the non-CAD status of the concept are stated plainly.
Testing covers measurement, power topology, DAW and NVMe thermal loads, fan failures, obstruction, noise, airflow, cable loads, signal integrity, RF, and safety.
The selected display, connector gutter, dual airflow lanes, rear heel, service architecture, and validation plan are mutually consistent.
arms.most_consequential_strength: Best reconciliation of the observed connector ambiguity with a coherent, serviceable thermal package.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The eight-key musician interface remains configurable and unlabeled rather than resolved around repeated workflows.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: Pi, cooler, NVMe, and fan specifications are detailed, but the assumed GPIO-mounted HyperPixel and custom hub do not account for the reported display-side USB-C connectors and require fit validation.
Commit-controlled repository facts, official hardware facts, inferences, assumptions, and unknowns are separated consistently.
Two aligned intake bands feed defined display and NVMe paths with a splitter, specified outlet area, sealing, and optional loaded-filter testing.
The rear fan has independent fused power, open-drain PWM, tach monitoring, and fail-full-speed behavior without disturbing the Active Cooler header.
Direct recessed power and video access, plug envelopes, cable anchors, dust shutters, and retention of the stock PCIe route handle connector motion comprehensively.
A removable electronics cassette, captive bottom, separate fan hatch, service door, and filter access preserve the permanently installed cooler.
Five HID keys plus touch, mouse, keyboard recovery, USB audio and MIDI support are useful, but the actual key mapping and repeated musical workflow are deferred.
The response is candid about component assumptions, installed acoustic uncertainty, backlight behavior, and unproven thermal, structural, and manufacturing claims.
The risk table defines concrete fit, thermal, failure, acoustic, power, UI, shutdown, stability, and dust tests under relevant loads.
The compact four-inch concept, GPIO display stack, port layout, two-lane cooling, custom controller, and service procedure are internally aligned despite their assumptions.
arms.most_consequential_strength: Highly integrated compact design with unusually thorough fan-failure, recovery-input, and validation provisions.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: Its display and custom USB-controller baseline remains speculative and does not reconcile the reported extra USB-C hardware.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: The adaptable display carrier avoids falsely identifying unknown hardware while accurately specifying the Pi, cooler, NVMe reference, and interface inventory.
Verified facts, reasonable inferences, explicit assumptions, and the unresolved two-USB-C observation are separated clearly.
The large filtered intake, quantified NVMe split, display and cooler wash, rear reunion, leakage seals, and serviceable filter form a complete path.
Native cooler control remains independent while the exhaust fan receives fused PWM control, tach monitoring, warning behavior, and a defined escalation policy.
Connector orientation and raceways are thoughtful, but the high-current USB-C panel pigtail and full-size HDMI adapter add motion, voltage-drop, and signal-integrity risks.
Replaceable display and Pi carriers, captive access panels, a sliding cassette, independent filter removal, and permanent cooler retention strongly preserve untouched parts.
Eight tactile keys, replaceable legends, landscape presentation, ballast, and mapping tests help repeated use, but actual musical functions and recovery behavior are not resolved.
The design openly identifies surrogate hardware, provisional dimensions, extension risks, and all unproven performance claims.
Validation includes hardware audit, power integrity, display mapping, dual-ambient thermal soak, multiple faults, smoke testing, acoustics, service cycles, safety, and wireless checks.
Modular carriers, rear cable gallery, airflow routing, structure, assembly sequence, and service approach consistently support the selected decoupled architecture.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The most disciplined treatment of unidentified display hardware through modular carriers and explicit uncertainty.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The selected power and HDMI panel extensions create avoidable electrical and mechanical risk at the most critical connectors.

comparative_result: Harbor ranks first at 39/40. Ember, Quartz, and Willow tie at 38/40. All four are unusually strong in airflow, fan separation, maintenance, evidence honesty, verification, and coherence; Harbor leads by best reconciling the reported connector ambiguity without accepting a high-current power extension.
disagreements: The principal tradeoff is hardware interpretation: Harbor assigns the reported USB-C connectors to a clearly assumed display, Willow deliberately leaves their identity unresolved, and Ember and Quartz choose display baselines that lack them. Willow's modular uncertainty handling is excellent, but its panel-mounted power path is less robust than the direct-access strategies.
